title: Launch on Product Hunt & directories
summary: The launch-day play: prep assets and copy, submit to Product Hunt and startup directories, rally your network, and track the signup spike.

parts.title: Prepare launch assets and copy
parts.guidance: Build the launch packet from the working product: description, intended audience, real screenshots or demo, logo, destination URL and answers to likely questions. Verify feature and customer claims against what is available at launch, and confirm rights to testimonials and customer assets. Adapt the copy to the selected channel so the launch owner can clear a concrete set of public claims and assets.

parts.title: Submit to Product Hunt
parts.guidance: Choose a launch venue that fits the product's readiness and intended audience. Check current eligibility, required assets, charges and submission rules. Test the destination and arrange for a product representative to answer questions. Submit the launch owner's agreed content and timing within the authorized fee, then track whether the submission is awaiting review or actually published.

options.title: Default — Submit to Product Hunt
options.summary: Complete Product Hunt's current submission form with the launch packet, tested product URL, tagline, imagery and maker identity. Confirm the publication or scheduling decision with the launch owner. Check the resulting listing and have a maker answer genuine questions. Share it within Product Hunt's promotion rules; coordinated voting and incentives for upvotes are prohibited.

references.title: How do I share my post?

verify.how: The launch is scheduled in your Product Hunt dashboard and the post URL resolves publicly on launch day.

options.title: Show HN launch
options.summary: Use Show HN when the maker has a substantive project that people can actually try and is available to discuss it. The guidelines exclude landing pages and signup-only material and ask for an accessible demonstration. Have the maker write, approve and manually post their own submission, starting its title with Show HN, and handle the discussion personally under the current HN rules. Save the post link and feedback; soliciting upvotes or comments is prohibited.
options.when: Developer-tool audience - Show HN reaches it better than Product Hunt

options.title: BetaList pre-launch
options.summary: Check BetaList's eligibility for the product and its own-domain landing page; its criteria cover upcoming and recently launched startups. Prepare an accurate description, visuals and working signup or access path. Before the authorized purchase, resolve the package price and refund terms against checkout and the applicable terms, including discrepancies in published guidance. Keep the receipt and editorial status separate from evidence that a feature has been published.
options.when: Pre-launch - you want waitlist signups before the product is public

parts.title: Submit to startup directories
parts.guidance: Choose directories that serve the intended audience and check their eligibility, terms and charges. Adapt the launch description without changing its claims or destination. Submit to the agreed destinations within the paid-listing budget. Track each review status and published URL, then check live listings for accurate copy and working links so corrections can be requested where needed.

parts.title: Rally your network on launch day
parts.guidance: Share the launch link through the agreed company or community channels and have someone answer product questions from experience. Tailor the outreach to each venue's rules: Product Hunt prohibits coordinated voting and upvote incentives, while Hacker News prohibits soliciting upvotes or comments. Collect substantive feedback and route reported product failures to the team that can fix them.

references.title: How do I share my post?

parts.title: Track the signup spike
parts.guidance: Compare launch traffic and signups with a defined pre-launch baseline. Check referral attribution, duplicate events and the signup funnel before crediting a listing. Follow signups through activation or the next meaningful product action. Report results by channel and observation window, including tracking gaps and customer feedback, so the team can choose follow-up experiments from outcomes beyond the initial traffic spike.

metadata.supportReason: Asset prep and analytics are agent work. The submission portals have no launch APIs, and rallying your network on the day is human.
